venue.name: Jamie's Whaling Station & Adventure Centres - Ucluelet
venue.description: Jamie's Whaling Station runs boat based wildlife tours from its own office and marina at 168 Fraser Lane in Ucluelet, one of the company's two West Coast locations. From Ucluelet the trips go into Barkley Sound to look for grey and humpback whales and for black bears feeding along the shore at low tide, either on the 12 passenger cabin cruiser Pacific Springs or on open 12 passenger Zodiacs, and each trip runs 2.5 to 3 hours. Guided sea kayaking tours leaving from Ucluelet are sold on the same website but are run by Paddle West Kayaking, which the site says is a separate company. The site says the Ucluelet location takes children 3 years and older, and that nobody under 4 feet 8 inches can ride a Zodiac.

facility_notes.bus_parking: In Ucluelet, there is parking in front of the Jamie's building as well as along the roads near our offices. All parking is FREE in these areas.
facility_notes.washrooms: Our larger vessels all have washrooms onboard for use. On our smaller vessels including our Zodiacs, we have small marine toilets that are for emergency use only.
facility_notes.rain_backup: Our tours are Rain or Shine and we ask that you check the forecast prior to arriving for your departure and dress accordingly.
facility_notes.lunch_space: For all tours except bear watching tours, you are allowed to bring your food and drinks with you.

restrictions: Our Ucluelet location offers Whale and Bear watching trips for those 3 years and older.
Anyone under the height of 4’8″ (142cm) is also unable to join our Zodiac tours.
We do ask that any guest under the age of 19 travels with a supervising adult.

For our bear watching tours, we ask that you do not bring any food or drinks other than water as bears have a strong sense of smell and we do not want the bears to associate us with food in any way for their health and safety.
No running, jumping, screaming, or climbing railings is permitted.

We do not recommend this tour to anyone with a history of serious medical conditions. These include, but are not limited to, anyone who is pregnant, those with back, neck or knee problems, osteoporosis, incontinence, recent surgery or limited mobility.
Emotional support or therapy dogs are not permitted on board.
All tours are subject to the signing of a waiver releasing Jamie's Whaling Station from liability.
venue.hours_notes: Check-in is 30 minutes prior to your departure time. Bear watching departure times vary from day to day based on low tide times when bears emerge from the forest to forage for shellfish.
venue.seasonal_notes: The Ucluelet whale watching season is given as early February through October for 2026. The Ucluelet bear watching season is given as mid-April through September. Kayaking from Ucluelet runs daily March to September. Fall and winter tours run from the Tofino location only.

programs.name: Ucluelet Covered Cruiser Whale Watching
programs.description: A 2.5 to 3 hour whale watching trip from Ucluelet into Barkley Sound aboard a covered cabin cruiser with indoor heated seating, an open rear deck and a marine toilet. The Ucluelet cruiser is the Pacific Springs, listed on the fleet page as carrying 12 passengers and suitable for ages 3 and up. Grey whales and humpbacks are the usual sightings, with sea lions, seals, sea otters and eagles along the way. If the boat does not see a whale, everyone on board gets a Raincheck Ticket for a free second tour.
programs.what_children_do: Sit in a heated cabin and watch through the big windows, then step out onto the open deck at the back of the boat when the skipper finds whales. The skipper gives commentary about the whales and the coast the whole way out and back.
programs.our_note: It is two and a half to three hours on a boat with no way to get off, so it suits children who can settle in a seat. Boats have to stay 100 metres back from whales, so binoculars make a real difference. Allow about an extra hour on top of the tour for checking in beforehand and getting off afterwards.
programs.practical_summary: There is a toilet on the boat and washrooms at the office, parking in front of the building is free, and the heated cabin means rain does not end the trip. Nothing about a school or daycare rate, a group booking route or bus parking is on the site, so it is worth a call.
programs.extra_fees_note: On top of the listed rates, checkout adds 5% GST, a $2 port fee, a $1 research, rescue and education fee per person, a $5 fuel surcharge, and a 6% booking fee on online bookings. Youth 13 to 18 pay $157.94 and seniors 65 and over pay $168.54.
programs.cancellation_note: Whale watching tours have a 48 hour cancellation policy. Anything cancelled inside 48 hours, including dropping the number of passengers, is not refunded. Outside 48 hours you get the whole amount back.

programs.name: Ucluelet Zodiac Whale Watching
programs.description: A 2.5 to 3 hour whale watching trip from Ucluelet on an open 12 passenger Zodiac with forward facing seats. Flotation suits are provided. The page states a height requirement of 4 feet 8 inches or 142 centimetres to ride, and lists the tour as unsuitable for anyone pregnant or with back, neck or knee problems, osteoporosis, incontinence, recent surgery or limited mobility. The emergency marine toilet is listed as currently unavailable. The page does not publish a minimum age, only the height rule.
programs.what_children_do: Put on a full body flotation suit, sit in a forward facing seat on an open boat and hold on for a fast ride out along the coast of Barkley Sound, stopping to watch whales and other wildlife. Everyone stays in their seat for the whole trip.
programs.our_note: The height rule is the thing to check first, because 142 centimetres rules out most children under about nine regardless of the ticket price. There is no usable toilet on board and no shelter from wind or spray, so this is a harder trip than the cruiser for a young group.
programs.practical_summary: Flotation suits are provided and parking at the Ucluelet office is free, but there is no toilet on the boat and no cover from the weather. The site does not say what the youngest age is for this boat, only the height limit, so ask before you book.
programs.extra_fees_note: On top of the listed rates, checkout adds 5% GST, a $2 port fee, a $1 research, rescue and education fee per person, a $5 fuel surcharge, and a 6% booking fee on online bookings. Youth 13 to 18 pay $157.94 and seniors 65 and over pay $168.54.
programs.cancellation_note: Whale watching tours have a 48 hour cancellation policy. Anything cancelled inside 48 hours, including dropping the number of passengers, is not refunded. Outside 48 hours you get the whole amount back.
programs.evidence: Must be at least 4'8" / 142cm in height to ride on the Zodiac

programs.name: Ucluelet Cabin Cruiser Bear Watching
programs.description: A 2.5 to 3 hour black bear watching trip from Ucluelet along the shoreline of Barkley Sound aboard a cabin cruiser with indoor heated seating, an open rear deck and a marine toilet. Departures are set by the low tide, so the time changes from day to day. The price list states that infants aged 0 to 2 are not permitted on the tour. No food or drink other than water may be brought on a bear tour. If the boat does not see a bear, everyone gets a Raincheck Ticket for a free second tour.
programs.what_children_do: Ride a heated cruiser into calm inlet water at low tide and watch the rocky shore for black bears flipping stones over to find crabs and clams, with the crew pointing out eagles, seals and sea lions along the way.
programs.our_note: Departure times follow the tide rather than the clock, so the slot you get may not fit around naps or pick up. Food is not allowed on a bear trip, water only, which is a long stretch for small children. Seasickness is unlikely here because the boat stays in sheltered water.
programs.practical_summary: There is a toilet on the boat, free parking at the Ucluelet office and a heated cabin, but no food is allowed on board and the departure time moves with the tide. A group rate, a group booking route and bus parking are not published, so plan on a phone call.
programs.extra_fees_note: On top of the listed rates, checkout adds 5% GST, a 6% booking fee on online bookings, a $2 port fee, a $1 research, rescue and education fee per person and a $5 fuel surcharge. Youth 13 to 18 pay $157.94 and seniors 65 and over pay $168.54.
programs.cancellation_note: Bear watching tours have a 48 hour cancellation policy. Anything cancelled inside 48 hours, including dropping the number of passengers, is not refunded. Outside 48 hours you get the whole amount back.
programs.evidence: Infant Ages 0-2 are NOT permitted on tour

programs.name: Ucluelet Zodiac Bear Watching
programs.description: A 2.5 to 3 hour black bear watching trip from Ucluelet on an open 12 passenger Zodiac. The page states a height requirement of 4 feet 8 inches or 142 centimetres, and the price list states that infants aged 0 to 2 are not permitted. Departures follow the low tide. No food or drink other than water may be brought on a bear tour.
programs.what_children_do: Put on a flotation suit, sit in an open boat and travel along the shoreline at low tide watching for black bears turning over rocks to find crabs.
programs.our_note: Between the height rule and the no food rule this is a hard fit for a young group, and the cabin cruiser version of the same trip is the gentler choice. Departure times move with the tide, so ask what time you would actually be leaving before you commit.
programs.practical_summary: Flotation suits are provided and parking is free, but there is no proper toilet on board, no cover from the weather, and no food allowed. The height limit and the tide driven departure time are both worth settling on the phone.
programs.extra_fees_note: On top of the listed rates, checkout adds 5% GST, a 6% booking fee on online bookings, a $2 port fee, a $1 research, rescue and education fee per person and a $5 fuel surcharge. Youth 13 to 18 pay $157.94 and seniors 65 and over pay $168.54.
programs.cancellation_note: Bear watching tours have a 48 hour cancellation policy. Anything cancelled inside 48 hours, including dropping the number of passengers, is not refunded. Outside 48 hours you get the whole amount back.

programs.name: Ucluelet Whale & Bear Package
programs.description: A package of two separate Ucluelet tours, one whale watching and one bear watching, which can be taken on the same day or on different days. Each tour is 2.5 to 3 hours. The listing says ages 3 and up. The site shows only a starting price for the package and no breakdown by age, so the cost for a child is not recorded here.
programs.what_children_do: Two boat trips in Barkley Sound, one out towards open water looking for grey whales and humpbacks, and one tucked into calm water at low tide watching black bears forage along the shore.
programs.our_note: Two boat trips of nearly three hours each is a lot for small children, so splitting them across two days is worth asking for. The price shown on the site is a starting figure with no child rate beside it, so get a quote before you count on it.
programs.practical_summary: It is two separate boat trips of 2.5 to 3 hours each, bookable on the same day or apart. The actual price per child is not published, so ask for a quote when you call.
programs.evidence: Trips can either be on the same day or separate days depending on your preference. Each tour is 2.5 to 3 hours long.

programs.name: Ucluelet Harbour Kayaking Tour
programs.description: A 2.5 hour guided sea kayak tour of the sheltered Ucluelet harbour, marked beginner friendly and priced the same for every age at $87.98. The site says it is run by Paddle West Kayaking, which it describes as a separate company from Jamie's. Kayaks, paddles, dry bags, personal flotation devices and spray skirts are provided. Groups are usually no more than six paddlers with a guide, and a tour needs at least two guests to run. There is a washroom on site at check-in.
programs.what_children_do: Sit in the front of a double kayak with an adult behind and paddle around the harbour for about two and a half hours, stopping to float over kelp and look at seals, sea stars, herons and eagles while the guide explains what lives in the intertidal zone.
programs.our_note: Children start at five and sit in front with one adult behind, so in practice you need close to one adult per child unless the guide takes one. This one is run by Paddle West Kayaking rather than Jamie's, so their 24 hour cancellation rule applies and not the 48 hour one on the boat tours. They paddle in the rain, so pack rain gear rather than expecting a postponement.
programs.practical_summary: There is a washroom on site at check-in, the price is the same for adults and children, and everything but clothing is provided. Nothing about a school or daycare rate is published, and seating children needs an adult per kayak, so call before you plan numbers.
programs.extra_fees_note: On top of the listed rate, checkout adds 5% GST and a 6% booking fee on online bookings.
programs.cancellation_note: There is a 24 hour cancellation and rebooking policy for kayak day tours, and a 48 hour one for groups larger than six people. Inside 24 hours the full amount is charged, and rebooking inside 24 hours costs $20 a person.
programs.evidence: Our minimum age is 5 years old in order to join one of our tours.

programs.name: Ucluelet Coast Kayaking Tour
programs.description: A 4 hour guided sea kayak tour that leaves the shelter of Ucluelet harbour for the shoreline of northern Barkley Sound, priced the same for every age at $130.38 and run by Paddle West Kayaking. The site says beginners are welcome but that paddlers must be comfortable in ocean swell and unprotected water and able to paddle for 30 to 45 minutes without a rest. There is a stop on land for a lunch you pack yourself.
programs.what_children_do: Paddle out of the harbour into open swell for about four hours, along rocky shore and small islets, with rest stops and a stop on land to eat a packed lunch.
programs.our_note: The ask here is real: paddling 30 to 45 minutes at a stretch in ocean swell is a lot for an eight year old, and the harbour tour is the gentler version of the same idea. Lunch is not provided, so everyone brings their own.
programs.practical_summary: Four hours on open water with a land stop for a packed lunch, at one flat price for all ages. There is no published school or daycare rate and no stated group maximum, so call to sort numbers.
programs.extra_fees_note: On top of the listed rate, checkout adds 5% GST and a 6% booking fee on online bookings.
programs.cancellation_note: There is a 24 hour cancellation and rebooking policy for kayak day tours, and a 48 hour one for groups larger than six people.
programs.evidence: You must be comfortable with paddling in ocean swell and in unprotected waters

programs.name: Ucluelet Barkley Sound Kayaking Tour
programs.description: A 6 hour guided sea kayak tour from Ucluelet out of the harbour into the open swell of northern Barkley Sound, run by Paddle West Kayaking and booked by phone rather than online. The site lists it at $167 a person. The page gives two different minimum ages, 12 and up in the tour details and 4 and up in the price list. There is a stop on land for a lunch you pack yourself.
programs.what_children_do: Paddle for most of a day in open ocean swell along rugged shoreline and islets, watching for seals, sea lions and eagles, with a stop on land to eat a packed lunch.
programs.our_note: Six hours in open swell is a trip for confident older paddlers rather than a class outing. The age on this page is given two different ways, so settle it on the phone before anyone counts on coming.
programs.practical_summary: Six hours on open water, booked by phone, at $167 a person with a packed lunch of your own. The minimum age is published two different ways on the same page, so confirm it when you call.
programs.extra_fees_note: On top of the listed rate, checkout adds 5% GST and a 6% booking fee on online bookings.
programs.cancellation_note: There is a 24 hour cancellation and rebooking policy for kayak day tours, and a 48 hour one for groups larger than six people.

programs.name: Private tour from Ucluelet
programs.description: A private boat for one group, bookable with Ucluelet as the departure point through an inquiry form on the site. The Ucluelet whale and bear pages list a private tour for up to 12 people at CA$2,703, which matches the 12 passenger capacity of the Ucluelet cabin cruiser and Zodiacs. The private tours page separately says rates start at $850 an hour plus taxes and fees with a two hour minimum depending on the vessel, and the inquiry form offers passenger bands of 1 to 12, 13 to 30 and 31 to 45. The larger vessels named on the fleet page are based in Tofino, not Ucluelet.
programs.our_note: A private boat is the way to keep a group together and set your own timing, but the two prices on the site do not line up and the bigger boats are based in Tofino. Send the inquiry form with your group size and ask what a boat leaving from Ucluelet would actually cost.
programs.practical_summary: A private Ucluelet boat is listed at $2,703 for up to 12 people, and elsewhere at $850 an hour with a two hour minimum. There is a form for inquiries rather than an online checkout, and nothing about school or daycare groups is published.
programs.extra_fees_note: The private tours page says rates start at $850 per hour plus taxes and fees with a two hour minimum, depending on the vessel.
programs.evidence: Private Tour All Ages • Up to 12 People CA$ 2,703

gaps: the site never mentions school groups, daycare groups, classes or educational programs anywhere, so there is no school or group rate, no teacher contact and no curriculum material
no group discount is published; the only multi booking offer is $15 off per person for a second tour taken by the same guest
no minimum or maximum group size is published for a scheduled departure; the 12 passenger figure is the capacity of the Ucluelet vessels, so a group of 12 would fill a boat
no lead time or minimum notice is published; the site only recommends booking early for June to September and says large groups should book well in advance
no chaperone ratio is published; the only rule is that guests under 19 must travel with a supervising adult
the Ucluelet Whale & Bear Package shows only a starting price with no breakdown by age, so no child price is recorded for it
the tour listing cards all show the same starting price of CA$179.14 regardless of age, which does not match the child prices on the tour pages, so card prices were not used
no wheelchair or stroller access information is published for the Ucluelet office, the dock or either vessel type
bus parking is not mentioned; the site describes free car parking in front of the Ucluelet building and on nearby roads
no indoor lunch space is described at the Ucluelet office; food is allowed on board on whale tours and banned on bear tours
no rain backup is offered; the site says tours are rain or shine and only cancels for unsafe sea conditions
the Ucluelet office opening hours are not published, only that check-in is 30 minutes before departure
departure times are not published for any Ucluelet tour; bear tour times change daily with the low tide
the Ucluelet Zodiac whale watching page publishes a height requirement but no minimum age, so age_min_years is left null for that tour

bear watching months from Ucluelet are uncertain: the Ucluelet bear page says mid-April through September, the home page says April 15 to October 15 and the FAQ says April through October, recorded in conflicts
whale watching start month is uncertain: the Ucluelet whale page says early February and the home page says March, recorded in conflicts
the kayaking tours sold from the Ucluelet pages are run by Paddle West Kayaking, which the site says is a separate company, with its own cancellation policy
the Ucluelet bear cabin cruiser page names the Eagle 44 as an Ucluelet cabin cruiser, while the fleet page lists the Eagle 44 as based in Tofino

the page banner images on the Ucluelet pages are CSS background images with no alt text and no descriptive file names, so they were not recorded; the images kept here all carry the site's own alt text
no languages other than English are mentioned for tours

conflicts.note: Their own pages give different answers for when bear watching runs from Ucluelet. One says mid April to the end of September, another says April 15 to October 15. If you are looking at late September or October, check the dates when you book.

Two of their pages disagree about when whale watching starts in Ucluelet. The Ucluelet page says early February, the home page says March. Worth settling when you book if you want an early spring date.

The site says the Ucluelet boats take children 3 and older, but the private tour listing says all ages. If anyone under three is coming, ask whether they can be on an Ucluelet boat at all before you plan around it.

The six hour kayak tour from Ucluelet is listed as ages 12 and up in the tour details and ages 4 and up in the price list on the same page. It is a long trip in open ocean swell. Settle the age on the phone before you book.
